teaser: Our own email connector: one gateway agent touches Gmail, everyone else works on a signed twin of the mailbox in a vault, with policies at five altitudes.
core_idea: Separate reading from sending: one gateway agent holds the Gmail token, the mailbox becomes a vault twin that people and agents work on through signed lanes, and policies apply at every altitude.

nodes.label: The usual connector
nodes.summary: No enforcement, no policies, no context.

nodes.label: One gateway agent
nodes.summary: The only holder of the token.

nodes.label: A twin in a vault
nodes.summary: The mailbox as signed, encrypted files.

nodes.label: Five altitudes of policy
nodes.summary: From the OAuth grant to one email's content.

quotes.text: The design rests on one idea: only one agent ever touches Gmail.
That leaves a digital trail of attention, not only of action.
The fourth altitude is the new one.

figures.caption: The email agentic cell: one gateway touches Gmail; people and agents work on a twin in a vault.
Four flows: connect, receive, work together and send, each step signed, each send through the gateway.
Behaviour policies at five altitudes, from the OAuth grant to what a single email may say.
The email cell's features: from a shared inbox with roles to an inbound firewall, signed mail and a calendar twin.
